Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Reno NV
157 AM PST Sun Nov 22 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

* Periods of light valley rain and snow continue through tonight,
  with minor travel impacts in the Sierra.

* Holiday travel will be most ideal Monday into Tuesday, disrupted  
  by another weaker storm Tuesday night or Wednesday. 

* Dry and mild weather is favored for Thanksgiving Day, with 
  additional storms possible next weekend and beyond. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...

A weak Pacific storm will continue to deliver periods of light rain 
and snow into this evening before showers clear out later tonight.
Snowfall totals remain quite meager with this storm, adding up to
2" along the Sierra crest -- especially around the Tahoe Basin. 
Even the higher end scenarios (10% chance) only show 2-4" along 
highest mountain peaks by Monday morning. Elsewhere, expect a 
trace to 1" locally beneath the heavier snow showers -- except on 
valley floors where a rain-snow mix would, at most, allow a trace 
of snow on grassy or elevated surfaces. 

Clearing skies should allow for pockets of freezing fog across NE 
California and E Sierra valleys tonight into early Monday morning. 
Low clouds and patchy fog may develop overnight in Reno and the 
Carson Valley, but this would be more dependent on light rain/snow 
this evening. 

Transient high pressure will provide another break between storms
Monday into Tuesday afternoon, offering the most ideal window for
holiday travel through the mountains before the arrival of our 
next storm Tuesday night. This storm has trended much weaker in 
latest guidance with snowfall totals resembling those from our 
ongoing storm: 70% chance of 2-3" along the Sierra crest, 70-90% 
chance of 1-2" at pass level, 60-90% chance of a trace at 
Truckee/lake level and along/west of US-395 in Mono County. 
Moreover, snow levels are projected to lift from 5000-5500 ft to 
near 7000 ft during the storm's duration, suggesting a switch from
snow to rain would occur below Sierra passes sometime Wednesday. 

Meanwhile, W Nevada valley communities would likely only see rain 
with this storm, although the coldest scenarios would support light 
snow on valley floors Wednesday morning (10% likelihood). The bigger 
issue would be getting showers to spill into W Nevada as guidance
hints at a pronounced shadowing effect. Winds are also expected 
to increase on Tuesday in response to the approaching storm, with 
SW gusts of 25-35 mph near the Oregon border and across E Sierra 
valleys. Ridgetop winds may gust up to 80 mph at times. Expect 
wind impacts to backcountry and lake recreation, with turbulent 
flights into and out of regional airports on Tuesday.

A quick trough passage to the north will bring low shower chances
to areas near the Oregon border on Thanksgiving Day, otherwise 
the holiday and the Friday after are favored to be dry and mild. 
Ensembles remain keen on unsettled weather to end November and 
welcome December, with another storm possible next weekend (Nov 
28-29). 

-Salas

&&

.AVIATION...

KRNO Forecast: VFR conditions and light winds prevail this morning, 
with SW FL100 of 30 kts supporting minor LLWS and mountain wave 
turbulence concerns through 13Z this morning. Low chances (20-30%) 
of -RASN between 22Z and 02Z, which may reduce CIGS/VIS to MVFR 
conditions and obscure surrounding mountain terrain. Low clouds or 
patchy FZFG is possible Monday morning -- especially if light 
showers develop close to/after sunset, but chances of FZFG/IFR 
conditions at the airfield is low at 10% or less. 

Regional Outlook: Periods of -SN will occasionally lower CIGS/VIS
to near IFR conditions at KTRK-KTVL, especially between 22Z and 
03Z. -RASN may reduce CIGS/VIS to MVFR conditions (20-30% chance) 
and obscure surrounding mountain terrain at KCXP and KMEV between 
22Z and 03Z. A SW belt of 30 kt FL100 flow will maintain minor 
LLWS and mountain wave turbulence at all area terminals until 13Z.
FZFG likely develops at KTRK tonight into early Monday, resulting
in periods of LIFR conditions. 

24-72 Hour Outlook: High pressure allows for widespread VFR 
conditions Monday and most of Tuesday. Another storm will bring 
increased winds, mountain snow, and valley rain late Tuesday and 
Wednesday, impacting busy air travel. 

-Salas
